correctness.rationale: Each Arens extension depends linearly and isometrically on the underlying bounded bilinear map, so the discrepancy operator \(D(h)=h^{\square}-h^{\diamond}\) is linear with norm at most \(2\). The reverse triangle inequality gives the Lipschitz estimate, and comparison with any regular product gives the distance bound. In the explicit \(\ell_1\oplus_1\ell_1\oplus_1\mathbb C\) algebra, every triple product vanishes and the triangular sign matrix has opposite iterated ultrafilter limits \(1\) and \(-1\), so \(\Delta_A=2\) at multiplication norm one. The zero multiplication is regular at distance one, proving both sharpness statements.
correctness.risk: The exact norm calculations are tied to the fixed Banach-space norm; no claim is made about renorming-invariant notions.

value.rationale: The proposed defect is natural, but the substantive theorem beyond the explicit example is a direct norm-triangle calculation: the \(2\)-Lipschitz law is immediate from two norm-one extensions, and the distance-to-zero-set inequality is the standard consequence for any Lipschitz defect. The triangular sign matrix is a classical double-limit mechanism for Arens irregularity. Under the common value bar, packaging these routine facts into a named gap with a sharpness witness does not add enough mathematical structure to qualify as a worthwhile new result.
value.risk: The quantitative formulation can still be pedagogically useful, but expository convenience is not the scientific-value criterion.

final_claim: For a bounded bilinear multiplication \(m\), the Arens-product discrepancy \(\Delta_A(m)=\|m^{\square}-m^{\diamond}\|\) is globally \(2\)-Lipschitz in the multiplication norm, gives the lower bound \(\operatorname{dist}(m,\mathcal R_{\mathrm{alg}})\ge\Delta_A(m)/2\), and both constants are sharp even for an associative cube-zero algebra.
limitations: This rejection is for scientific value, not correctness.
The originality assessment remains best-of-knowledge because the closest recent primary full text was inaccessible.
